new.analysis:
Nothing from the week of Sep 21 – 27 gives me a training signal, so next week restarts from where the plan stopped. No runs were recorded and all three planned sessions (24, 24 and 27 minutes) show as missed. Your sleep was 7.5 hours, stress was low and your body felt fine, so nothing in your check-in points to a physical reason.

Repeating the missed week is better than catching up. Your last recorded run was Sat Sep 19, so Monday comes after a nine-day gap. That costs a fit beginner little, but it is long enough to ease back in. Only three of the last five weeks have had all three runs, so your legs have not had a long stretch of steady work yet.

For you, the build phase means longer run segments, not hard sessions. You are about four weeks into running, so every run stays easy and there is no threshold work yet. Threshold work would add risk without helping you run 5K without stopping. The step that matters is stretching each run from 2 minutes towards continuous running.

I want the run segments slower because the goal is time on your feet, not speed. Roughly half your recent heart-rate time has landed in zone 3, even though the walk breaks sit in zone 2. You also told me the 2-minute runs were hard. A slower shuffle costs you nothing at the finish line and lets the run segments grow sooner.

Six weeks is tight but realistic if the next few weeks are complete. If you finish all three runs next week, the week of Oct 5 – 11 moves to 3-minute runs with 1-minute walks, and later weeks stretch from there. By the week of Oct 26 I want you running around 10 minutes without a walk break. If you are not close, we adjust the race plan to something honest rather than rush the progression.
